dossier.public_summary: The signal looks like a flat-bottomed dip but the measured depths swing by a factor of two between odd and even events and by a factor of >10 between TESS sectors and between individual transits, with two or three very deep outliers driving the detection. That pattern is best explained by background variability or an eclipsing binary blended in the light, not a single transiting planet on the target M dwarf.

reasons.why: Strong odd/even depth difference indicates two different eclipse depths folded at half period (~27.4 d vs 13.7 d), not a single planet transit.
Depth changes dramatically between sectors: 1963, 8336, 34268 ppm vs -155 ppm and is confirmed as changes_within_a_source, inconsistent with a planet.
Individual transit depths are wildly inconsistent; the entire folded signal is dominated by 2-3 abnormally deep events, not a coherent planetary transit.
reasons.value: 1.065e-128 (share_of_top_3 0.991, mean_depth_ppm 6455, outliers 39728 ppm at sigma 15.5, 30021 ppm at sigma 12.5, -1321 ppm)

reasons.why: On-target centroid is not confirmed while odd/even and depth-variability evidence favor an EB/blend/variable-star false alarm.
reasons.value: inconclusive (why: no sector with a clear difference image)
